title: Stashing Work & Release Tagging
description: Shelve unfinished changes temporarily with git stash and mark milestone releases with lightweight and annotated tags.

blocks.content: An urgent fix arrives while your half-finished experiment is still open. You need to set work aside without committing it. What is the smallest Git action that keeps the work safe?

A stash stores uncommitted changes temporarily. `git stash push -m "note"` sets work aside, and `git stash pop` restores it when you are ready.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Working files"] -->|"choose an action"| B["Git history"] -->|"share or recover"| C["Team project"]
```

blocks.question: When is a stash useful?
options: When unfinished work must be set aside temporarily
When you want to publish a release
When you need to merge branches
When you want to delete history
blocks.explanation: A stash keeps uncommitted work recoverable without making it a commit.

blocks.prompt: Model the Git idea in a tiny simulator. Export a function named `stashFile` that takes `(working, staged, file)` and returns a new staged list containing `file` once. Do not change either input list.

tests.description: works when no working files are listed yet
keeps an already staged file while adding another
